scores.claim_text: In fiscal 2025, 68% of total revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. Government.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts (Mode A: 'Kratos Defense'; Mode B: 'Kratos Unmanned' subsidiary roll-up)
scores.M_value: Mode A: 494 awards, total_amount $1.672B obligated. Mode B: 'Kratos Unmanned' alone shows 174 awards / $1.123B; combined federal obligations across Kratos legal entities materially exceed 68% of FY25 total revenue of $1.347B (implied federal-revenue ~ $915M). Top contracts include BQM-177A SSAT full-rate production ($238.8M), CCS-C C2 production ($206M / $310M), and BQM-167 sub-scale aerial target.
scores.interpretation: PASS: Federal obligated $$ at multiple Kratos subsidiaries comfortably support the 68% federal revenue concentration claim. Mode B subsidiary resolution confirms the rollup.

scores.claim_text: Remaining performance obligations of $1,573.4M as of Dec 28, 2025 (54% recognizable in 2026).
scores.M_check: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form (Mode A: 10-K on file 2026-02-23); usaspending recipient federal obligations vs RPO scale (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: 10-K accession 0001069258-26-000013 filed 2026-02-23 confirms disclosure. Mode B: cumulative federal obligations across Kratos entities (~$1.67B-$2.04B in DoD contracts) are larger than the $1.57B RPO; the gap is in the right direction (obligations > RPO, since RPO measures unburned-down execution). No material divergence indicating phantom backlog.
scores.interpretation: PASS: RPO disclosure is plausibly supported by the federal-contract obligation base. Heuristic 10 (IDIQ ceilings vs obligated $$) not violated — federal obligated $$ comfortably exceed RPO.

scores.claim_text: Kratos is a DoD prime with revenue across named programs (XQ-58 Valkyrie, Zeus SRM, Erinyes, Sentinel ICBM-related).
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts (Mode A); pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding for each named program (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: 579 DoD contracts to Kratos totaling $2.04B obligated — overwhelming PASS for general DoD-prime claim. Top awards confirm BQM-177A SSAT full-rate production ($238.8M), CCS-C ($310M), BQM-167 sub-scale aerial target. Mode B: Pentagon JBOOK shows Collaborative Combat Aircraft (PE 0207147F) FUNDED_SHRINKING — FY24=$0M, FY25=$711.7M, FY26=$111.4M (an 84% reduction in newest PB). XQ-58 Valkyrie, Zeus, Erinyes, Sentinel, BQM-167, BQM-177 returned NOT_FOUND in the J-Book corpus (program names may map to other PEs or are below corpus coverage).
scores.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: Mode A is a strong PASS (Kratos is clearly a DoD prime with billions in obligated DoD contracts on target-drone programs). However, Mode B surfaces a material forward-looking caveat: the CCA program (where Kratos pitches Valkyrie & GE-Aerospace engines) shows 84% funding reduction FY25-FY26 in the newest PB. An obligated past-year contract is NOT the same as forward-funded program; the CCA wind-down in PB26 is a SEVE-flavored Mode B finding even though existing target-drone obligations are robust.

scores.claim_text: Formal teaming agreement with GE Aerospace for engines for next-gen unmanned aerial systems and CCA-type aircraft, including planned Oklahoma turbofan facility.
scores.M_check: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form 8-K (Mode A); edgar_fts.query_fulltext in GE CIK 0000040545 (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: 30+ Kratos 8-Ks on file across the window — disclosure cadence consistent with a material partnership announcement (specific 8-K identification deferred). Mode B: edgar_fts.query_fulltext for 'Kratos' inside GE Aerospace CIK 0000040545 returned n_hits=null (FTS endpoint returned no usable hits; cannot confirm or deny GE-side disclosure of Kratos via this index).
scores.interpretation: UNVERIFIABLE: edgar_fts returned no result rather than zero hits — appears to be an index coverage / endpoint issue rather than a true absence-of-disclosure finding. Per heuristic 7, counterparty-disclosure SEVE requires a clean zero-hit on a working query; we cannot conclude that here. Tag as UNVERIFIABLE rather than over-call SEVE.

scores.claim_text: Material stock issuance for acquisitions and registered resales (Nomad Feb 2026 $88M+; Norden $32M); active acquirer with stock-as-consideration cadence.
scores.M_value: Mode A: S-3ASR filings present (2026-02-26, 2024-02-21, 2023-10-04, 2021-02-10, 2021-02-09) and 424B5 prospectus filings 2026-02-27, 2026-02-26, 2025-06-27, 2025-06-25, 2024-02-23 — confirms repeated public/secondary offerings, including a 424B5 ONE DAY after the 2026 10-K filed. Mode B: insider_vs_calendar over 2024-01-01 to 2026-05-20 with window_days=14 returned 122 Form 4 filings, 373 total insider sales, $160.4M sale value, and **80 proximate sales worth $31.5M near budget events, of which 78 are DISCRETIONARY (non-10b5-1) across 9 unique insiders**. Matched events: 47 discretionary sales worth $27.5M in the 14-day window around the Jan 20, 2026 bipartisan budget signing (incl. CEO Eric DeMarco selling 189,824 shares @ $90.27 = $17.1M on Jan 6, 2026 — non-10b5-1, 14 days before budget signed); 16 discretionary sales worth $1.85M around fiscal-year-end 2025-09-30; 15 discretionary sales worth $2.23M around the FY27 J-Book release 2026-04-28. Per the Two-Mode DD Discipline framework: 'CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY signal: that is the highest-signal flag → SEVE or RED.'
scores.interpretation: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY: Discretionary insider selling is densely clustered to calendar-knowable Pentagon/budget catalysts. The Jan-2026 cluster ($27.5M, 9 insiders, 47 discretionary sales in a 14-day window) coincides with the bipartisan budget signing and pre-empts the CCA PB26 funding shrinkage (711.7M→111.4M) that is also visible in this run's Mode B. CEO DeMarco's $17.1M discretionary sale 14 days before the Jan-20 budget catalyst is the single highest-signal data point. Per framework rubric, this is a SEVE flag; would be RED with additional confirmation of explicit Pentagon-program disclosure asymmetry.
